# Command reference

Every generated command, with the OSDU operation behind it. `osducs <noun> --help` shows the
same information at the terminal, and is the authority if the two ever disagree.

Commands are named for the **resource**, not the service that hosts it, so verbs live under
the thing they act on: searching records is `osducs record search`. See
[COMMAND-GRAMMAR.md](COMMAND-GRAMMAR.md) for why.

Hand-written commands — `osducs status`, `osducs record add`, `osducs file upload`,
`osducs file download`, `osducs completion` — are not listed here, since no manifest describes
their options; `record add` is in [USAGE.md](USAGE.md#writing-records), and the file commands in
[USAGE.md](USAGE.md#files). Neither are `group list`'s `--all` and `--type`, added by hand; see
[USAGE.md](USAGE.md#operations). Run `osducs --help` for the full tree.

Each command says what it **requires**: the roles its service's spec documents, which are also
what `--help` and a refused request show. They are what the spec says, not a guarantee; a
deployment may differ, and ADME answers some refusals with 401 rather than 403.


| Noun | Commands |
|---|---|
| [`action`](#action) | `get`, `add`, `test`, `match`, `delete` |
| [`crs`](#crs) | `get`, `transform`, `area-of-use`, `convert`, `convert-trajectory`, `convert-geojson` |

## Commands that need an operator role

Every role that admits these is an admin or ops role, such as `users.datalake.ops`, `users.datalake.admins` or a `service.*.admin`, which data users do not usually hold. Everything else a data user's viewer or editor groups admit, where the spec says.

| Command | Requires |
|---|---|
| [`osducs action add`](#osducs-action-add) | users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins |
| [`osducs action delete`](#osducs-action-delete) | users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins |
| [`osducs dataset revoke-url`](#osducs-dataset-revoke-url) | service.dataset.admin |
| [`osducs ddms delete`](#osducs-ddms-delete) | users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins |
| [`osducs file revoke-url`](#osducs-file-revoke-url) | service.file.admin |
| `osducs group list --all` (hand-written) | users.datalake.ops or service.entitlements.admin |
| [`osducs index delete`](#osducs-index-delete) | users.datalake.ops |
| [`osducs index provision`](#osducs-index-provision) | users.datalake.ops |
| [`osducs index reindex`](#osducs-index-reindex) | service.search.admin |
| [`osducs index reindex-partition`](#osducs-index-reindex-partition) | users.datalake.ops |
| [`osducs index reindex-records`](#osducs-index-reindex-records) | service.search.admin |
| [`osducs record list`](#osducs-record-list) | service.storage.admin |
| [`osducs record purge`](#osducs-record-purge) | service.storage.admin |
| [`osducs record replay`](#osducs-record-replay) | users.datalake.ops |
| [`osducs record replay-status`](#osducs-record-replay-status) | users.datalake.ops |
| [`osducs subscription delete`](#osducs-subscription-delete) | users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins |
| [`osducs workflow add`](#osducs-workflow-add) | service.workflow.admin |
| [`osducs workflow delete`](#osducs-workflow-delete) | service.workflow.admin |

## action

### `osducs action add`

Register an action from a JSON file.

`POST /action` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file with the action — name, url with {placeholders} filled from a record, and a filter of the records it is offered for. |

```bash
osducs action add --file action.json
```

### `osducs action delete`

Delete an action registration.

`DELETE /action/{id}` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Action registration id. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the action registration `<id>`. Records no longer offer it.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs action delete --id "open-in-petrel"
```

### `osducs action get`

Get an action registration by id.

`GET /action/{id}` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops, users.datalake.admins, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Action registration id. |

```bash
osducs action get --id "open-in-petrel"
```

### `osducs action match`

The registered actions offered for a record, with their urls filled from it.

`POST /action:retrieve` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops, users.datalake.admins, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file with the record, or the fields of it the actions are filtered and filled by. |

```bash
osducs action match --file record.json
```

### `osducs action test`

Check how an action would fill its url from a sample record, without registering it.

`POST /action:test` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops, users.datalake.admins, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file with the action and a testPayload, the record to fill its url from. |

```bash
osducs action test --file action-test.json
```

## crs

### `osducs crs area-of-use`

Check which transformations are valid for a set of points.

`POST /v3/points-in-aou` — crs_catalog

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the points and the transformations to test. |

### `osducs crs convert`

Convert a list of points to another coordinate reference system.

`POST /v4/convert` — crs_conversion

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the points and the target CRS. |

### `osducs crs convert-geojson`

Convert a GeoJSON structure to another coordinate reference system.

`POST /v4/convertGeoJson` — crs_conversion

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the GeoJSON or AnyCrsGeoJson structure. |

### `osducs crs convert-trajectory`

Convert wellbore trajectory stations to another coordinate reference system.

`POST /v4/convertTrajectory` — crs_conversion

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the trajectory stations and the target CRS. |

### `osducs crs get`

Get a coordinate reference system by record or data id.

`GET /v3/coordinate-reference-system` — crs_catalog

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--record-id` |  | CRS record id. |
| `--data-id` |  | CRS data id. Give this or --record-id. |

> One of `--record-id` or `--data-id` is required.

### `osducs crs transform`

Get a coordinate transformation by record or data id.

`GET /v3/coordinate-transformation` — crs_catalog

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--record-id` |  | Transformation record id. |
| `--data-id` |  | Transformation data id. Give this or --record-id. |

> One of `--record-id` or `--data-id` is required.

## dataset

### `osducs dataset add`

Create or update dataset registry records from a JSON file.

`PUT /registerDataset` — dataset

Requires service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the dataset registry records. |

### `osducs dataset delete`

Soft-delete a dataset metadata record.

`POST /metadataRecord/{id}/softDelete` — dataset

Requires service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Dataset metadata record id. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the dataset record `<id>`. `dataset undelete` restores it.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs dataset download-url`

Get instructions for reading a dataset's bytes.

`GET /retrievalInstructions` — dataset

Requires service.dataset.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Dataset registry record id. |
| `--expiry` |  | How long the instructions stay valid, e.g. 5M or 2H. |

### `osducs dataset get`

Get a dataset registry record by id.

`GET /getDatasetRegistry` — dataset

Requires service.storage.creator, service.storage.admin or service.storage.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Dataset registry record id. |

### `osducs dataset revoke-url`

Revoke previously issued dataset URLs.

`POST /revokeURL` — dataset

Requires service.dataset.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind-subtype` | yes | Dataset sub-type whose URLs should be revoked. |
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file naming the resource whose URLs should be revoked. |

### `osducs dataset undelete`

Restore a soft-deleted dataset metadata record.

`POST /metadataRecord/{id}/undelete` — dataset

Requires service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Dataset metadata record id to restore. |

### `osducs dataset upload-url`

Get instructions for writing a new dataset's bytes.

`POST /storageInstructions` — dataset

Requires service.dataset.editors.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind-subtype` | yes | Dataset sub-type, e.g. dataset--File.Generic. |
| `--expiry` |  | How long the instructions stay valid, e.g. 5M or 2H. |

## ddms

### `osducs ddms add`

Register a DDMS from a JSON file holding its OpenAPI 3 description.

`POST /ddms` — register

Requires users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file with the registration — id, name, contactEmail and interfaces. |

```bash
osducs ddms add --file ddms.json
```

### `osducs ddms delete`

Delete a DDMS registration.

`DELETE /ddms/{id}` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops or users.datalake.admins — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | DDMS registration id. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the DDMS registration `<id>`. The platform no longer lists the DDMS; the DDMS itself is not touched.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs ddms delete --id "wellbore-ddms"
```

### `osducs ddms get`

Get a DDMS registration by id.

`GET /ddms/{id}` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops, users.datalake.admins, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | DDMS registration id. |

```bash
osducs ddms get --id "wellbore-ddms"
```

### `osducs ddms list`

List the DDMS registrations of a type.

`GET /ddms` — register

Requires users.datalake.ops, users.datalake.admins, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.viewers.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--type` | yes | Type of entity the DDMS serves, e.g. wellbores. |

```bash
osducs ddms list --type wellbores
```

## file

### `osducs file add`

Register metadata for a file already uploaded to the landing zone.

`POST /v2/files/metadata` — file

Requires service.file.editors, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the file metadata record. |

### `osducs file delete`

Delete a file and its metadata record.

`DELETE /v2/files/{id}/metadata` — file

Requires users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.admins.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | File metadata record id to delete. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the file record `<id>` and the stored file it describes.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs file download-url`

Get a signed URL to download a file from.

`GET /v2/files/{id}/downloadURL` — file

Requires service.file.viewers, users.datalake.viewers, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | File metadata record id. |
| `--expiry` |  | How long the URL stays valid, e.g. 5M for five minutes or 2H for two hours. |

### `osducs file get`

Get the metadata record for a file.

`GET /v2/files/{id}/metadata` — file

Requires service.file.editors, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | File metadata record id. |

### `osducs file revoke-url`

Revoke previously issued signed URLs.

`POST /v2/files/revokeURL` — file

Requires service.file.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file naming the resource whose URLs should be revoked. |

### `osducs file upload-url`

Get a signed URL and landing-zone location to upload a file to.

`GET /v2/files/uploadURL` — file

Requires service.file.editors, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--expiry` |  | How long the URL stays valid, e.g. 5M for five minutes or 2H for two hours. |

## group

### `osducs group add`

Create a group.

`POST /groups` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Group name, without the partition suffix, e.g. users.datalake.viewers. |
| `-d`, `--description` |  | What the group is for. |

### `osducs group delete`

Delete a group.

`DELETE /groups/{group_email}` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-g`, `--group` | yes | Group email address. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the group `<group_email>`. Its members lose the access it gave them.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs group list`

List the groups you belong to, or with --all every group in the data partition.

`GET /groups` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--role-required` |  | Include the caller's role in each group. |

```bash
osducs group list 
```

### `osducs group member add`

Add a member to a group.

`POST /groups/{group_email}/members` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-g`, `--group` | yes | Group email address. |
| `-m`, `--member` | yes | Email address of the user or service principal to add. |
| `--role` | yes | Role to grant the member. |

### `osducs group member count`

Count the members of a group.

`GET /groups/{group_email}/membersCount` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-g`, `--group` | yes | Group email address. |
| `--role` |  | Count only members with this role. |

### `osducs group member delete`

Remove one member from one group.

`DELETE /groups/{group_email}/members/{member_email}` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-g`, `--group` | yes | Group email address. |
| `-m`, `--member` | yes | Member email address to remove. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Remove `<member_email>` from `<group_email>`.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs group member list`

List the members of a group.

`GET /groups/{group_email}/members` — entitlements

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-g`, `--group` | yes | Group email address. |
| `--role` |  | Return only members with this role. |
| `--include-type` |  | Include each member's type in the output. |

## index

### `osducs index delete`

Delete the search index of a kind.

`DELETE /index` — indexer

Requires users.datalake.ops — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-k`, `--kind` | yes | Kind whose index to delete, e.g. osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the search index of `<kind>`. Its records stay in Storage, but searches for the kind find nothing until it is re-indexed.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs index delete --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0"
```

### `osducs index provision`

Provision the Indexer for the data partition.

`PUT /partitions/provision` — indexer

Requires users.datalake.ops — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Provision the Indexer for the data partition, which is done once when a partition is set up.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs index reindex`

Re-index every record of a kind from Storage.

`POST /reindex` — indexer

Requires service.search.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--force-clean` |  | Delete the kind's index first and rebuild it from scratch, as a changed mapping needs. Until it finishes, searches for the kind find only what has been re-indexed. |
| `-k`, `--kind` | yes | Kind to re-index, e.g. osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. With --force-clean, the command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead, when `--force-clean` is given: *Delete the search index of `<kind>` and rebuild it from Storage. Until it finishes, searches for the kind find only what has been re-indexed.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs index reindex --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0"
```

### `osducs index reindex-partition`

Re-index every kind in the data partition from Storage.

`PATCH /reindex` — indexer

Requires users.datalake.ops — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--force-clean` |  | Delete each kind's index first and rebuild it from scratch. Until it finishes, searches find only what has been re-indexed. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Re-index every kind in the data partition from Storage, a long job for the Indexer and Elasticsearch. With --force-clean every index is deleted first, and searches find only what has been re-indexed until it finishes.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs index reindex-records`

Re-index specific records from Storage.

`POST /reindex/records` — indexer

Requires service.search.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id` | yes | Ids of the records to re-index, at most 1000. Repeat the flag or comma-separate. |

```bash
osducs index reindex-records --id "opendes:master-data--Well:1000,opendes:master-data--Well:1001"
```

List all versions of a WellboreIntervalSet record.

`GET /ddms/v3/wellboreintervalsets/{record_id}/versions` — wellbore_ddms

Requires users.datalake.viewers, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.admins.

## record

### `osducs record aggregate`

Count distinct values of a field across matching records.

`POST /query` — search

Requires users.datalake.viewers, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-k`, `--kind` | yes | Kind to aggregate over. Wildcards allowed per segment. |
| `-b`, `--by` | yes | Field to count distinct values of, e.g. kind. Only fields indexed as keywords can be aggregated; others answer "Aggregations are not supported for one or more of the specified fields". |
| `-q`, `--query` |  | Lucene query to narrow what is counted, e.g. data.FacilityName:GB*. |

```bash
osducs record aggregate --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--*:*" --by kind
osducs record aggregate --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --by kind --query 'data.FacilityName:GB*'
```

### `osducs record delete`

Soft-delete a record by id.

`POST /records/{id}:delete` — storage

Requires service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id to delete. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the record `<id>`. Storage keeps its versions until it is purged, and the deletion can be reverted.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs record get`

Get the latest version of a record by id.

`GET /records/{id}` — storage

Requires service.storage.viewer, service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id. |
| `-a`, `--attributes` |  | Restrict the returned fields of the record. |

```bash
osducs record get --id "opendes:master-data--Wellbore:1000"
```

### `osducs record headers`

Fetch record headers by id, without the data payload.

`POST /query/records/headers` — storage

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id. Repeat the flag for up to 1000 records. |
| `-a`, `--attributes` |  | Header fields to return. Omit for all of them; 'id' is always included. |

```bash
osducs record headers --id "opendes:master-data--Wellbore:1000" -a kind -a acl
```

### `osducs record list`

List records of a given kind.

`GET /query/records` — storage

Requires service.storage.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-k`, `--kind` | yes | Kind of records to list. |
| `-l`, `--limit` |  | Maximum number of records to return. |
| `--cursor` |  | Cursor returned by a previous page. |

```bash
osducs record list --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.2.0" --limit 5
```

### `osducs record purge`

Permanently delete a record and every version of it.

`DELETE /records/{id}` — storage

Requires service.storage.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id to purge. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Permanently delete the record `<id>` and every version of it. This cannot be undone.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs record purge --id "opendes:master-data--Well:1000"
```

### `osducs record replay`

Send records from Storage to their consumers again, to rebuild the index or more.

`POST /replay` — storage

Requires users.datalake.ops — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--operation` | yes | reindex to send the records to the Indexer, or replay to publish them as record changes to every consumer, the Indexer included. |
| `-k`, `--kind` |  | The kind to replay; the service takes one. Without it, every kind in the data partition. |
| `--replay-id` |  | An id for the replay, to follow it by. The service makes one up when omitted. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. Without --kind, the command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead, unless `--kind` is given: *Replay every kind in the data partition from Storage, as a `<operation>`: a long job for Storage and everything that consumes its records.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs record replay --operation reindex --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0"
```

### `osducs record replay-status`

Show how far a replay has got; -o json breaks it down by kind.

`GET /replay/status/{id}` — storage

Requires users.datalake.ops — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Replay id, as `record replay` printed it. |

```bash
osducs record replay-status --id "f506be08-b51f-4cdd-a9ee-d9454ad51600"
```

### `osducs record search`

Search records with a Lucene query.

`POST /query` — search

Requires users.datalake.viewers, users.datalake.editors, users.datalake.admins or users.datalake.ops.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-k`, `--kind` | yes | Kind to search. Wildcards are allowed per segment, so "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" covers every schema version — pinning one silently misses records written against the others. |
| `-q`, `--query` |  | Lucene query string, e.g. data.FacilityName:GB* for a prefix, or data.FacilityName:"GB 211/23-A8" for an exact phrase. Omit to match everything of this kind. |
| `-l`, `--limit` |  | Maximum number of results. Defaults to 10. Above 1000, Search's per-request maximum, the results are fetched 1000 at a time through its cursor. |
| `--offset` |  | Number of results to skip. Search refuses --offset plus --limit beyond 10000, so results past the first 10000 cannot be reached this way. |
| `--sort-by` |  | Fields to sort by, e.g. id or data.FacilityName. Pair positionally with --sort-order. |
| `--sort-order` |  | Sort direction per --sort-by field. Defaults to ASC upstream when omitted. |
| `--track-total-count` |  | Report the true match count. Without it the count is capped at 10000, which silently understates any large kind. |
| `-f`, `--returned-fields` |  | Fields to project, e.g. id, data.FacilityName. Repeat the flag or comma-separate. These become the table columns, so asking for a field shows it. Server-side, so it also cuts what crosses the wire. |
| `-x`, `--excluded-fields` |  | Fields to omit, e.g. data.rawData — everything else is returned. Repeat the flag or comma-separate. The inverse of --returned-fields and cannot be combined with it. Columns stay Id and Kind unless --returned-fields names others, since an exclusion says nothing about what to show. |
| `--spatial-field` |  | Geo-point field to filter on. Required with --bbox or --near; the OSDU convention is data.SpatialLocation.Wgs84Coordinates. |
| `--bbox` |  | Bounding box as TOPLAT,TOPLON,BOTTOMLAT,BOTTOMLON — note top-left first, so the latitudes descend. Example: 49.1,7.7,48.8,8.0. |
| `--near` |  | Centre point as LAT,LON, e.g. 48.935251,7.865344. Pair with --within. |
| `--within` |  | Radius in metres around --near. |
| `--all` |  | Return every match, fetched 1000 at a time through /query_with_cursor. Cannot be combined with --limit or --offset. |

> `--returned-fields` and `--excluded-fields` cannot be combined.

> `--bbox` and `--near` cannot be combined.

```bash
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --limit 5
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:work-product-component--WellLog:*" --limit 2500 -f id
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --limit 3 -x data.GeoContexts -x data.NameAliases
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --spatial-field data.SpatialLocation.Wgs84Coordinates --bbox 49.1,7.7,48.8,8.0 --limit 3 -f id -f data.FacilityName
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --spatial-field data.SpatialLocation.Wgs84Coordinates --near 48.935251,7.865344 --within 50000 --limit 3 -f id -f data.FacilityName
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --query 'data.FacilityName:GB*' --limit 5
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --query 'data.FacilityName:"GB 211/23-A8"'
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --limit 5 -f id -f data.FacilityName
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --limit 5 --sort-by id --sort-order DESC
osducs record search --kind "osdu:wks:master-data--Well:*" --limit 1 --track-total-count
```

### `osducs record version get`

Get a specific version of a record.

`GET /records/{id}/{version}` — storage

Requires service.storage.viewer, service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id. |
| `-v`, `--version` | yes | Record version. |
| `-a`, `--attributes` |  | Restrict the returned fields of the record. |

### `osducs record version list`

List all versions of a record.

`GET /records/versions/{id}` — storage

Requires service.storage.viewer, service.storage.creator or service.storage.admin.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id. |

### `osducs record version purge`

Permanently delete versions of a record, keeping the latest.

`DELETE /records/{id}/versions` — storage

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | Record id. |
| `--version-ids` |  | Versions to delete, comma-separated. Cannot be combined with --limit or --from. |
| `-l`, `--limit` |  | How many versions to delete; the service's limit parameter. |
| `--from` |  | The version to delete from; the service's from parameter. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> One of `--version-ids` or `--limit` or `--from` is required.

> `--version-ids` and `--limit` cannot be combined.

> `--version-ids` and `--from` cannot be combined.

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Permanently delete versions of the record `<id>`, keeping its latest. This cannot be undone.* `--yes` skips the question.

```bash
osducs record version purge --id "opendes:master-data--Well:1000" --limit 5
```


> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the record `<record_id>`. Records that refer to it are not deleted with it.* `--yes` skips the question.

## welllog

### `osducs welllog add`

Add a WellLog record from a JSON file.

`POST /ddms/v3/welllogs` — wellbore_ddms

Requires users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.admins.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the WellLog record. |

### `osducs welllog data get`

Read the bulk data of a WellLog record.

`GET /ddms/v3/welllogs/{record_id}/data` — wellbore_ddms

Requires users.datalake.viewers, users.datalake.editors or users.datalake.admins.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |
| `--offset` |  | Row to start at. |
| `-l`, `--limit` |  | Maximum rows to return. |
| `--curves` |  | Comma-separated columns to return, e.g. MD,GR. Omit for all. |
| `--filter` |  | Row filter as column:operator:value, e.g. MD:gte:1000. Operators: lt, lte, gt, gte, eq, neq. |
| `--describe` |  | Return row and column counts instead of the data. |
| `--orient` |  | JSON shape of the response. |

### `osducs welllog data session get`

Get a bulk data upload session of a WellLog record.

`GET /ddms/v3/welllogs/{record_id}/sessions/{session_id}` — wellbore_ddms

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |
| `-s`, `--session` | yes | Session id, as session open printed it. |

```bash
osducs welllog data session get --id "opendes:work-product-component--WellLog:1000" --session "4b2e1c3a-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
```

### `osducs welllog data session list`

List the bulk data upload sessions of a WellLog record.

`GET /ddms/v3/welllogs/{record_id}/sessions` — wellbore_ddms

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |

```bash
osducs welllog data session list --id "opendes:work-product-component--WellLog:1000"
```

### `osducs welllog data session open`

Open a session to send a WellLog's bulk data in chunks, then commit it with session update.

`POST /ddms/v3/welllogs/{record_id}/sessions` — wellbore_ddms

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |
| `--mode` | yes | overwrite to replace the bulk with what the session sends, or update to merge it into the version the session starts from. |
| `--from-version` |  | Version to start from with --mode update. The latest when omitted. |
| `--ttl` |  | Minutes the session stays open before it is dropped, at most 1440 (the default). |

```bash
osducs welllog data session open --id "opendes:work-product-component--WellLog:1000" --mode overwrite
```

### `osducs welllog data session update`

Commit a session, making what it sent a new version of the WellLog, or abandon it.

`PATCH /ddms/v3/welllogs/{record_id}/sessions/{session_id}` — wellbore_ddms

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |
| `-s`, `--session` | yes | Session id, as session open printed it. |
| `--state` | yes | commit to make what the session sent a new version, or abandon to drop it. |

```bash
osducs welllog data session update --id "opendes:work-product-component--WellLog:1000" --session "4b2e1c3a-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" --state commit
```

| Option | Required | Description |

| `-id`, `--id` | yes | WellLog record id. |
| `--curves` |  | Comma-separated columns, e.g. MD,GR. Omit for all. |

## workflow

### `osducs workflow add`

Register a workflow definition from a JSON file.

`POST /v1/workflow` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the workflow definition. |

### `osducs workflow delete`

Delete a workflow definition by name.

`DELETE /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.admin — an operator role.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name to delete. |
| `--yes` |  | Go ahead without asking. The command says what it is about to do and asks first, and refuses when there is no terminal to ask at. |

> Says what it is about to do and asks before going ahead: *Delete the workflow `<workflow_name>`.* `--yes` skips the question.

### `osducs workflow get`

Get a workflow definition by name.

`GET /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name. |

### `osducs workflow list`

List workflows registered in the partition.

`GET /v1/workflow` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--prefix` |  | Return only workflows whose name starts with this. |

### `osducs workflow run get`

Get one workflow run.

`GET /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}/workflowRun/{runId}` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name. |
| `-r`, `--run` | yes | Run id. |

### `osducs workflow run latest`

Show execution detail for the most recent task of a run.

`GET /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}/workflowRun/{runId}/latestInfo` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name. |
| `-r`, `--run` | yes | Run id. |

### `osducs workflow run list`

List the runs of a workflow.

`GET /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}/workflowRun` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name. |

### `osducs workflow run trigger`

Start a new run of a workflow.

`POST /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}/workflowRun` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.creator.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name to run. |
| `-f`, `--file` | yes | JSON file containing the run request, including its executionContext. |

### `osducs workflow run update`

Update the status of a workflow run.

`PUT /v1/workflow/{workflow_name}/workflowRun/{runId}` — workflow

Requires service.workflow.viewer.

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-n`, `--name` | yes | Workflow name. |
| `-r`, `--run` | yes | Run id. |
| `--status` | yes | New status for the run. |
